---
title: "Before the session"
---

Two things are needed before the session, and each ends in something that you can check: the case study read, and the deck opened once on the machine that you will bring. Together they take about an hour, and there is nothing to install and nothing to register for.

## 1. The case study

[Read the case study](../../cases/eu-frames/index.qmd){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

The case study presents the original study, with its questions, data and selections, then SCORE and the Multi100 project, the five reanalyses and how their results were put on one scale. The session works on this case throughout and can give it only a few slides, so read it before you come. The [exercise overview](../../cases/eu-frames/exercise.qmd) adds the table of what the five analysts found.

## 2. The deck

[Open the deck](../../live/eu-frames-short.html){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"} [Open the browser lab at Task 1](../../cases/eu-frames/lab.qmd#task-1-setup){.btn .btn-outline-primary target="_blank"}

The deck of the session runs R inside your browser, with the data already in place, and its hands-on slides carry the cells of the tasks. Open it the evening before the session, on the machine and in the browser that you will bring, wait until the cell on its second slide shows a "Run Code" button, and run it. If it reports 270 rows, 27 countries and 10 years, you are set, and your browser keeps the files that the deck downloaded, which matters where the Wi-Fi of a venue is slow. If the deck does not load, try another browser, and tell the facilitator before the session; the browser lab, a page of this site, holds the same tasks outside the deck, as the fallback.

**By the start of the session** the deck loads on the machine that you will use, and you know what the claim is and how far apart the results of the five analysts are.
